facts.raw_span: A 60-year-old woman presented with a 3-month history of epigastric abdominal pain
unintentional 33 lb weight loss
intermittent melena
her abdomen was soft and nontender without organomegaly
normocytic anemia with a hemoglobin level of 11.6 g/dL
An abdominal CT scan was unremarkable
a 1.5 cm semipedunculated polyp (Paris Isp) in the gastric body
the same color as the surrounding mucosa, with a smooth surface lacking overlying mucus or prominent vessels
a heterogeneous surface pattern with uniform pitting near the base
no ulcerations or depressions were noted
irritable bowel syndrome
diet-controlled gluten intolerance

concepts.why: The patient has a 1.5 cm semipedunculated polyp in the gastric body with a heterogeneous surface pattern.
The patient has normocytic anemia and intermittent melena, suggesting chronic blood loss.
The patient has melena and a gastric polyp, which may be the source of bleeding.
The patient has unintentional weight loss and diet-controlled gluten intolerance, suggesting malabsorption.
The patient has a history of irritable bowel syndrome.
The patient has a gastric polyp with a heterogeneous surface pattern, which may be malignant.

rationales.F01: Epigastric abdominal pain is a nonspecific symptom that could be related to gastric polyp or gastrointestinal bleeding.
rationales.F02: Unintentional weight loss is a concerning symptom that could be related to malabsorption, gastrointestinal bleeding, or gastric adenocarcinoma.
rationales.F03: Intermittent melena is a strong indicator of gastrointestinal bleeding.
rationales.F05: Normocytic anemia is a common finding in iron deficiency anemia, which could be caused by gastrointestinal bleeding.
rationales.F07: The presence of a gastric polyp is a strong indicator of the disease.
rationales.F11: Irritable bowel syndrome is a distinct diagnosis that is not directly related to the other concepts.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient presented with a 1.5 cm semipedunculated polyp in the gastric body, which was completely resected, and this finding directly explains the intermittent melena and normocytic anemia, making it the most specific and direct diagnosis.
